newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes off low, market may try higher.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes off low, market may try higher.

text.p: Gold prices fell to a new 3-1/2 year low on Wednesday but then rebounded on buying on the Comex futures market in New York.
"It might have a bit of upside potential this afternoon but the weakness is not over yet," one dealer said.
Bullion fixed at $354.45 per ounce in the London afternoon, up from the morning's $352.45, its lowest since October 4, 1993.
After being called to open lower, Comex February gold posted gains and showed $1.70 ahead at $356.40 at the fixing.
"A volume seller on the exchange yesterday has bought a bit back today," a dealer said explaining the firmer tone.

"Given what he did yesterday the floor is not going to let him out cheaply," the dealer added. Investment fund-led selling in New York on Tuesday and later in Hong Kong was sparked by the U.S. dollar climbing to a 30-month high against the mark, a modest increase in U.S. inflation and continuingly strong equity markets.
There were plenty of shorts still about "agonizing" over whether or not to cover if the market showed signs of going very much higher, the dealer added.
The market's sentiment, which has been weak and nervous for months, turned morbidly gloomy this week after the Dutch central bank announced it had sold 300 tonnes of gold from its reserves.

Jitters persisted despite a statement on Monday from Hans Tietmeyer, chairman of the central bank governors of the so-called G10 group of leading economies, that they did not plan to sell gold for the time being.
"Nobody in the market is interpreting literally what a central bank says any more," one analyst said.
Dealers said it was unlikely gold's bounce would get much over $356.00 where there was a temporary floor on Tuesday.

The $350 area should provide some psychological support short term. But over time, prices were likely to target $330, the approximate lows from 1993, said technical analyst Elli Gifford at Investment Research of Cambridge..
The other precious metals were marked up from morning levels behind gold but dealers said there was only marginal interest.
Silver was still a cent under its previous close at $4.69/$4.71, platinum was down $3.70 at $359.80/$360.80 and palladium was $1.50 lower at $120.00/$121.00.
